newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Chidambaram to speak if parliament calm.
newsitem.headline: India's Chidambaram to speak if parliament calm.

text.p: Finance Minister P. Chidambaram will give his reply in parliament on Friday on the federal budget if proceedings are not disturbed over political upheaval in the western Indian state of Gujarat, a finance ministry official said.
"Mr Chidambaram is in Delhi and is likely to speak if parliament proceedings are not hampered or adjourned," the ministry spokesperson told Reuters.
The Finance Minister was forced to postpone his speech, eagerly awaited by stock markets, earlier this week following an uproar in parliament.
Markets were expecting Chidambaram to offer concessions to industries which have lobbied his office since he presented the blueprint of 1996/97 (April/March) budget on July 22.

But members of the main opposition Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), in an uproar over a split in the Hindu nationalist party in Gujarat state, forced repeated adjournment of both houses of parliament on Tuesday.
The proceedings were disrupted on Wednesday as well on the same issue. Parliament was closed on Thursday due to a Hindu festival holiday.

BJP lawmakers were protesting against a decision by the deputy speaker of the Gujarat assembly to recognise a breakaway faction of the right-wing party, which has been shaken by rivalries in the western state.
